slides.text: When the velvet vault of heaven frayed and night began shedding its constellations, the task fell to Master Oryn. Armed with a thimble turned from comet bone and a spool of moonbeam filament, he climbed the great obsidian steppes to stitch falling stars back into the dark cloth before dawn broke. If a star slipped free and struck the earth, its light would curdle into cold soot, and an ancient virtue would vanish from the minds of mortal men.

One biting November midnight, a sapphire star—the Star of Mercy—tore loose from Orion’s belt and plummeted into the snowdrifts of the lower valley. Oryn descended the mountain in haste, following the blue trail of luminescence through the woods. He expected to find a crater of smoldering cinder. Instead, he found an orphaned street urchin sitting beneath an ancient oak, cradling the blinding jewel against his threadbare tunic like a newborn sparrow, weeping with quiet awe.

'Mortal child,' Oryn commanded gently, needle raised. 'Relinquish the jewel. Without it in the firmament, men will forget how to forgive.' The boy looked up, his tears shimmering with starlight. 'Please, sir,' the boy whispered, trembling from the frost. 'My mother froze last winter, and this is the first thing that has kept my ribs warm since she left.' Oryn stared at his silver needle, untied his velvet pouch, and for the first time in ten thousand years, sewed a decoy stone into the sky.
